quotes.speaker: Willie Cauley-Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Willie Cauley-Stein on his upbringing in Spearville, Kansas
quotes.excerpt: It was like a big playground, bro. The town was like a mile long both ways.
quotes.quote: It was like a big playground, bro. The town was like a mile long both ways, so you could ride your bike in 10 minutes from one side to the other. There was a lot of hometown stuff, everybody feed everybody. I was eating dinner at all the homies' cribs, and it was community, good community.

quotes.speaker: Willie Cauley-Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Willie Cauley-Stein on his limited soccer experience
quotes.excerpt: I played in two soccer games my whole life and it was because of my big brother.
quotes.quote: I played in two soccer games my whole life and it was because of my big brother. He was playing in some soccer league in Dodge City, and they needed a kid to play. So I was just sitting around watching Big Bro, and they let me play a couple times. I got to score one point, and then I was running down the side, bro, and some girl slid tackled me, tore me up, man. I had a cast on my leg and stuff, man. I was done. I said I'm cool, I'm cool off soccer.

quotes.speaker: Willie Cauley-Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Willie Cauley-Stein on his mother's career and support
quotes.excerpt: She got into some financial problems, so we had to go live with our grandparents.
quotes.quote: She always supported us in everything that we would do. From when we were born till probably first grade, we were going back and forth with her and our family. She got into some financial problems, so we had to go live with our grandparents till she got established. Now she's in her 22nd year being an orthodontist assistant. We seen her go to school, get all her stuff for that, and then 20 years, I mean, damn near. I was probably 10 when she started doing that, so the business.

quotes.speaker: Willie Cauley-Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Willie Cauley-Stein on his father's absence and his own role as a father
quotes.excerpt: I don't look at him like a father, but I respect him as, after being a father now.
quotes.quote: I don't look at him like a father, but I respect him as, after being a father now, I respect like what. At first, I had a little different feeling until probably I had my first kid and now I'm going through financial troubles and life, people dying, you go through hardship, you know, it's like whatever it is. But I now understand what it is. It wasn't us, it wasn't the kids, you know, it was the situation and it was, you know, sometimes it.

quotes.speaker: Willie Cauley-Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Willie Cauley-Stein recalls a local athlete who played for the New York Giants
quotes.excerpt: He was a football player for the New York Giants. Don't know his name, we have to look that up.
quotes.quote: We had one guy in our whole history besides me that's probably done a professional sport. He was a football player for the New York Giants. Don't know his name, we have to look that up. But I was young, it's probably like 70s, at least 70s. They put his little helmet up, little picture and stuff in the gym, so that was, I was probably junior high, high school, that's where we seen him. I'm like, damn, dude played in the league.

quotes.speaker: Willie Cauley-Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Willie Cauley-Stein on playing in the MYB basketball tournament
quotes.excerpt: We used to play tournaments, we was called MYB. Don't know what it stands for.
quotes.quote: We used to play tournaments, we was called MYB. Don't know what it stands for. It might be some Kansas stuff, but I don't know. For real, for real, we played, you used to play tournaments, we was called MYB. Don't know what it stands for. I played in that as like a third grader onto 6th, 7th grade, and then we got a new coach that came in my freshman year, and he was a little younger and took us to a camp in at K-State, one of the team camps that they put on there, and I was going crazy. I was going crazy, and so one of the guys for now is called MoKan Elite, you know, like Trey Young, Michael Porter Jr., they all played on that team, but we was the first team that got them into the Nike league.

quotes.speaker: Willie Cauley-Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Willie Cauley-Stein on his growth spurt and transition to center
quotes.excerpt: I grew like seven inches that summer going into freshman year.
quotes.quote: I grew like seven inches that summer going into freshman year. So I was playing point guard, and then that summer, you you playing center now. And so it was a it was a crazy little little shift in the high school.

quotes.speaker: Willie Cauley-Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Willie Cauley-Stein on his basketball influences
quotes.excerpt: Tim Duncan was a big, yeah, because my grandfather, he loved the bank shot, bro.
quotes.quote: Tim Duncan was a big, yeah, because my grandfather, he loved the bank shot, bro. He loved the banks, the middy bank shot, bro. So I'd be out there in the yard working the bank shot. I remember, I don't know, probably 8th grade, whenever I would get into some trouble or like, I don't know, feel bad or something, I'll go out in the yard, bro. I remember playing one-on-one against Tim Duncan for the last second shot, you know how that shit goes. But yeah, Tim Duncan, man, and then KD. KD, just because he was just like, I don't know, one of the parents was like, 'Man, you like Kevin Durant.' And I was like, 'Who?' I never I didn't even know who he was yet. I had to go look him up. So we went, I went, I was like, 'Damn, I kind of do look like KD.' Shit, hold up, he long as hell, about I was like, 'Shit.' So yeah, shout out KD, bro, big bro right there.

quotes.speaker: Willie Cauley-Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Willie Cauley-Stein on his college recruitment process
quotes.excerpt: I had a chance to play in college. Wasn't even like, I don't even think my mom parents thought.
quotes.quote: I had a chance to play in college. Wasn't even like, I don't even think my mom parents thought they could go to that far, the like how far we took it, but they was just college. Like, oh, you got a chance to go play at like KU or a K-State. They was they was geeked off of that, so our whole kind of thing was like my grandparents wasn't real strict, bro. There was like, you're going to play this sport. Like, there was a there was a point where I was all in on football, my freshman year. Like, I had that growth spurt, but like before that, bro, I was I was a better football player. I played quarterback and I got to like control the shit like, and it was fun for me.

quotes.speaker: Willie Cauley-Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Willie Cauley-Stein on his experience at K-State team camp
quotes.excerpt: One of the guys for now is called MoKan Elite, you know, like Trey Young, Michael Porter Jr.
quotes.quote: One of the guys for now is called MoKan Elite, you know, like Trey Young, Michael Porter Jr., they all played on that team, but we was the first team that got them into the Nike league. So that was like my era, that's my claim to fame for them. We ain't never won a Peach Jam, but I'm like, shit, we got them in that mode. Yeah, I got in there.

quotes.speaker: Willie Cauley-Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Willie Cauley-Stein on living with his coach Robin Lucas
quotes.excerpt: I was staying with the coach, his name was Robin Lucas, and I was staying at his house.
quotes.quote: I was staying with the coach, his name was Robin Lucas, and I was staying at his house. And it was just like, I think the Shields feel bad for me, because I'm this kid and I have to stay with the coach, and they got, you know, three kids and this nice crib, pool, and they like, 'Man, he could come he could come stay with us.' So, Senya, which is the his wife, I'm pretty sure probably talked him into it, like, 'Oh yeah, let this kid come stay with us for the big fellow, come on.'

quotes.speaker: Willie Cauley-Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Willie Cauley-Stein on his academic struggles in high school
quotes.excerpt: I had to go to a different school to from my transcripts, so I get my grades together.
quotes.quote: I had to go to a different school to from my transcripts, so I get my grades together, because I was just a D student at the time, just chilling, playing sports, whatever, playing Call of Duty till 5:00 in the morning and then had to go to school. I was one of them type of kids, bro, just doing like the bare minimum to play sports. And so they really turned turned my whole kind of mentality around.

quotes.speaker: Willie Cauley-Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Willie Cauley-Stein on his recruitment by Kentucky and other schools
quotes.excerpt: They came in late. So they came in our last AAU tournament.
quotes.quote: They came in late. So they came in our last AAU tournament, which is when we got like a unofficial word that they were interested. So at that time, it was K-State, Oklahoma State, Florida, Alabama, and then Kentucky came in late. So I already had a really good relationship with Alabama. Obviously, K-State, we had been there a bunch, and I'm an in-state kid, so like they had I think matter of fact, Brad Underwood had coached my dad in JuCo. So like there was already a big kind of connection there. So I really I felt comfortable with those, and then I just like Billy Donovan, bro, when I was there, Billy was cool, bro. I was a cool dude. I just didn't really like the Florida facilities. It just wasn't, it wasn't covered compared to like Kentucky. They building a new one and they showing you like, 'Hey, this is going to be yours. This is brand new. You're going to be the first people to ever even be in this spot.' I'm like, okay, that shit cold, like that shit different. Everybody else had cement walls and we got big screens and shit. I don't know, it was just different.

quotes.speaker: Willie Cauley-Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Willie Cauley-Stein on his first AAU tournament and recruitment
quotes.excerpt: My first summer with at the Shields place, I got invited to the Top 100 camp.
quotes.quote: My first summer with at the Shields place, I got invited to the Top 100 camp, and the Nike Hoop Jam. And so I had to skip the the Top 100 camp because I had a geometry final that I had to redo. I'm telling you the Shields had me on some shit, bro, so I had to skip the 100 camp to do this geometry shit. And she was very, yeah, she was very like, 'You're not going.' And I was like, 'Damn.'

quotes.speaker: Willie Cauley-Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Developing confidence and ball handling skills during high school years
quotes.excerpt: I'm seeing the work, I'm seeing what the work is doing of the ball handling skills
quotes.quote: The second camp, the Nike Hoop Jam, was my first. I got invited to the Stotamire camp after that, the LeBron camp. As I got older, junior year, I was going to LeBron and Stotamire camps, but I was still trying to figure out who I was as a hooper, honestly, because I'm getting in a transition stage of growth. I'm seeing the jumps, right? I'm like, 'One more year, I'm number one pick.' I'm leaking another year here, bro, I'm cold. We are a different type of player the next year. So, I'm seeing the work, I'm seeing what the work is doing of the ball handling skills, the shooting that we're doing, and I'm getting to go on the floor where I want to go instead of being told where you should be going. When you can get to the rack, the game starts to slow down to you. It's slowing down and I'm getting to speed it up how I want to speed it up.

quotes.speaker: Willie Cauley-Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Training with Larry Lewis and developing on-court versatility
quotes.excerpt: It was giving me the confidence to be able to just to dribble the ball
quotes.quote: I think Coach Cal can attest to this when I came to Sacramento. We started doing work with Larry Lewis, and people were looking at us crazy, like, 'Why are they doing that with him?' But it was giving me the confidence to be able to just dribble the ball. I'm not scared to dribble this to De'Aaron Fox real quick or turn it down because they are overplaying it, because I ain't never done it before on film. There were just situations that I started seeing come out that became little niches that I could put in the game.

quotes.speaker: Willie Cauley-Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Willie Cauley-Stein on his relationship with Coach Calipari
quotes.excerpt: He became my legal guardians and really took me in and showed me how to live, bro.
quotes.quote: He became my legal guardians and really took me in and showed me how to live, bro. Showed me how to really do this and he had like, uh, it's called it was called 68 Inside Sports. So, I mean, that was like the first time that training was real. Like we had like real training and like I wasn't just playing sports in the the yard or playing like seven-on-seven football against guys that don't play football. Yeah, no, it was crazy. I was I was out here now. Yeah, yeah, yeah. I'm out here now, and uh, yeah, so I think that was the building blocks of like a mentality to be a professional.

quotes.summary_phrase: Willie Cauley-Stein on his draft night experience
quotes.excerpt: I was 22 years old. Okay, so we was the same, we was like the same age.
quotes.quote: I was 22 years old. Okay, so we was the same, we was like the same age. Draft night was kind of like, uh, it was cool, don't get me wrong, it was nostalgic, it was great. But man, I was just burnt off losing in the championship. That's the only time in my life that I was scared, but this probably the only time in my life that I was scared.

quotes.speaker: Willie Cauley-Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Willie Cauley-Stein on the emotional toll of being traded
quotes.excerpt: It was the guys that would get traded that you been with and you was going to war with.
quotes.quote: It hurts, bro. It was the guys that would get traded that you been with and you was going to war with, and all of a sudden you leaving, or they leaving. All of a sudden you was with this guy every day for a whole year and all of a sudden you never even talk to them no more because you not in the same world anymore.

quotes.speaker: Willie Cauley-Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Willie Cauley-Stein on being denied a contract extension by Sacramento
quotes.excerpt: I was sick because I just put all this work in and I wanted to be there.
quotes.quote: I didn't get an extension from Sacramento. I was sick. I was sick because I just put all this work in and I wanted to be there. They turned down my qualifying offer. I was cool with the people, I didn't even care what they had going on in the front office, I just wanted to get what I thought I was worth and I could set my shit up and I could just hoop.

quotes.speaker: Willie Cauley-Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Willie Cauley-Stein on the Warriors' team culture and organization
quotes.excerpt: I got to be around Steph, Klay, and they was hurt at the time, but they still showed up.
quotes.quote: I really liked the Warriors. It was a very dark time, my partner just got killed, and then I didn't get the extension, so I'm scrambling to find a job. I got to be around Steph, Klay, and they was hurt at the time, but they still showed up. I got to see why they were the way they were. It felt like a hobby for those guys. They were super fans. It wasn't like we were trying to win, because we weren't, we were not playing for anything.

quotes.speaker: Willie Cauley-Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Willie Cauley-Stein on the difference between the Kings and Warriors organizations
quotes.excerpt: In Sacramento it felt like a hobby. For these guys, it's their day-to-day, they're super fans.
quotes.quote: In Sacramento it felt like a hobby. For these guys, it's their day-to-day, they're super fans. That's what it felt like. Like, I like this guy, so I want to go get this guy. It wasn't like we were trying to win, because we weren't, we're not playing for anything.

quotes.speaker: Willie Cauley-Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Willie Cauley-Stein on the difficulty of being traded and losing his role
quotes.excerpt: I'm going from starting 360 games to now you're the guy that has to show everybody you're a starter.
quotes.quote: I'm going from starting 360 games to now you're the guy that has to show everybody on this team that you're a starter now. So I had to start over. I felt like a rookie all over again. And I done been busting Dallas's ass for the whole time I've been in my whole career.

quotes.speaker: Willie Cauley-Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Willie Cauley-Stein on his biggest regret being a 'hooper' instead of a 'businessman'
quotes.excerpt: I was a hooper, I wasn't a businessman, and I think that's the most thing that I regret.
quotes.quote: I was a hooper, I wasn't a businessman, and I think that's the most thing that I regret is not staying at them little parties that they throw. I was a hooper, I wasn't a businessman. Now we kind of in a position where I need those people. I need those relationships.

quotes.speaker: Willie Cauley-Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Willie Cauley-Stein on the impact of losing his best friends and grandfather
quotes.excerpt: I went through like five deaths in my circle in a two, three-year span.
quotes.quote: I went through like five deaths in my circle in a two, three-year span and I didn't process not one of them deaths because I'm hooping. I'm not going to see my grandfather in hospice because I got a game in Utah. I'm missing out on these things because I'm playing the game of basketball, bro.

quotes.speaker: Willie Cauley-Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Willie Cauley-Stein on his addiction to painkillers and the need to escape reality
quotes.excerpt: I was trying to not feel nothing and I'm just trying to go to sleep.
quotes.quote: It got to an emotional standpoint where it was like I'm trying to not feel nothing and I'm just trying to go to sleep and go play the game and go back to sleep and not be around. I'm not going out no more, I'm not doing things that light me up like being in the culture. That shit laid me out, that shit made me want to play harder, like seeing people like show you love.

quotes.speaker: Willie Cauley-Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Willie Cauley-Stein on the lack of support for players struggling with mental health
quotes.excerpt: I seen people not get back for way less than what I was going through.
quotes.quote: I seen people not get back for way less than what I was going through. I was like, I'm supposed to go in there because I met some people that I could not attain my mentality that I have today without going through what they were. When I realized that shit at the time, it was the last time my grandmother, she had cancer, throughout that whole summer going into that me going in, she end up passing away December 7th. I went in December 9th.

quotes.speaker: Willie Cauley-Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Willie Cauley-Stein on the importance of having hobbies outside of basketball
quotes.excerpt: You got to have a different hobby, you got to have some sort of hobby that you like.
quotes.quote: I think you got to find something away from ball to to take your mind off of when things aren't going right in ball. You got to have a different hobby, you got to have some sort of hobby that you like to indulge in that's healthy, obviously, like a healthier one. I don't know, like mine's golf. Some people's is Pokemon cards. I know Derek Lively here with Dallas, like he's a big like Pokemon, one-piece card trader. It's really like some stock shit, bro, it's crazy.

quotes.speaker: Willie Cauley-Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Willie Cauley-Stein on his addiction to golf as a coping mechanism
quotes.excerpt: I just started to spend a lot of money on it, just like getting the memberships, spending money.
quotes.quote: I just started to spend a lot of money on it, just like getting the memberships, spending money on just going to play, and like it became an addiction because I'm replacing one addiction with this new thing of striking this golf ball. Like flushing a golf ball, bro, there's no, to this day I have not had a feeling in any sport that I ever played of like the closest thing is hearing a net snap when you hit a perfect shot.
